Article Title: Oil prices fall as rising supply outweighs Middle East tensions and fears of tanker attacks
Article Text:
Oil eases as Middle East supply worry subsides

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Oil prices plunged marginally on Tuesday, with the prospect of a global supply surplus taking precedence over concerns about attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East. The possibility of rising supplies has weighed on the market even as tensions continue to threaten energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the region.WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents, or 0.62%, to $91.87. Prices were quoted with a 10-minute delay.Earlier on Friday, the International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year. The agency attributed this outlook to Middle East exports recovering at a faster pace than global oil demand, despite attacks on shipping.However, the security situation in the region remains a concern. Attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have continued, keeping uncertainty around a major global oil-export route.Though, geopolitical concerns are still present, they no longer having as much influence on prices as the supply outlook.Meanwhile, OPEC held a virtual meeting on Monday to discuss its assessment of members' maximum sustainable production capacity.The review is an important exercise as it will help establish OPEC+ production quotas for 2027 and subsequent years.The broader OPEC+ alliance, which also includes oil-producing countries led by Russia, is set to meet on November 29. The meeting will focus on deciding the group's oil output policy for 2027.In another development, US crude inventories held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve declined to 276.4 million barrels last week, marking their lowest level since August 1982, according to Department of Energy data.The latest reduction is part of an agreement by the US to release 172 million barrels of oil from the reserve.
Article Summary: WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents,or 0.62%, to $91.87. International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year.

Article Title: US reveals how Megaspeed came under scrutiny and landed on Nvidia's 'no sell' list in 2025
Article Text:
Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia's partnership with Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed hit a roadblock in June 2025, when the chipmaker put it on its "no sell" list. The decision came after US investigators sought details of Nvidia's direct and indirect sales to its Asia-Pacific partner, according to information released by the US commerce and justice departments on Monday.The US investigation, however, had started much earlier, in 2024, after authorities flagged suspicious activity linked to the possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.The commerce department approached Nvidia in May 2025, seeking records of direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed. A month later, the company found itself on Nvidia's restricted sales list, the two departments said in a joint statement.The agencies said the probe was triggered by suspicious activity detected through monitoring of potential semiconductor diversion."After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the department of commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations," the agencies said, as cited by Reuters.The investigation moved beyond records and sales checks in June 2025, when US agents travelled to Megaspeed's premises with Singaporean law enforcement officials. They carried out an "on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed" and questioned Alice Huang, who was then the company's chief executive.The Justice Department subsequently took charge of the criminal investigation into Megaspeed, following the enforcement action.The two departments said they were making details of the case public despite the usual practice of not commenting on ongoing investigations, citing public interest.Megaspeed's dealings with Nvidia are not the only aspect of the company drawing suspicion. Its former executive Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman, has also come under scrutiny, with some US authorities suspecting links to Chinese espionage efforts. However, Beijing has continued to refute the allegations.The allegations gained attention following reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12. en unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang formally left the company on August 30, 2025. It also maintained that it had conducted a "legitimate and lawful business."Singapore's government had said last week that Alice Huang previously held three key positions at Megaspeed — chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers.Police found insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed offences related to suspected false declarations over server purchases. However, they warned her for knowingly providing inaccurate information that played down her role in the company.Singapore has barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country. Investigations involving Megaspeed and six other individuals are still underway, the home affairs ministry said.Meanwhile, Singapore's government said on Monday that it had agreed to continue discussions with Washington over the company.
Article Summary: N Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed in June 2025. US investigators sought details of Nvidia's direct and indirect sales to its Asia-Pacific partner. US investigation started much earlier, in 2024, after authorities flagged suspicious activity linked to possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.

Article Title: Trump’s Nvidia stake grew to as much as $62 million: Report
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Trump's Nvidia stake

White House response to questions over Trump's Nvidia holdings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘She may not be a spy,’ says Trump

US President Donald Trump has stood by Nvidia’s former boss Jensen Huang despite a string of personal scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.But there is another Nvidia connection drawing attention: Trump's own stock portfolio.His investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year, with financial disclosures suggesting that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million.The disclosures put Trump's Nvidia holdings under the spotlight as the company grapples with controversy surrounding Huang's resignation and its business dealings with China.Trump’s Nvidia holdings, estimated at between $615,000 and $1.3 million at the end of 2024, rose to as much as $62 million within the last year, according to financial disclosures reviewed by The Washington Post. However, these filings do not include trades made over the past two months, so the latest value of his holdings could be even higher, The Independent reported.But the value of his holdings is only part of the picture. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.A CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures found that his accounts had bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times.The transactions were worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million.The exact size of Trump's current stake, however, remains unclear. His disclosures report investments in broad dollar-value ranges rather than the actual number of shares held. Based on the holdings reported in August, his Nvidia investment would have been worth between $4.5 million and $57.7 million by midday Monday, when the stock was trading at around $157.The latest disclosures do not capture transactions from the past two months, making it difficult to establish how much Nvidia stock Trump currently owns.Trump's investment accounts sold between $500,001 and $1 million worth of Nvidia shares on May 18, the first Monday after his return from a China visit with Huang. The sale was part of a wider trading spree, with Trump disclosing more than 21,000 trades in 2025, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.The scale of Trump's Nvidia investments has also raised questions about his financial interests in the company, particularly given his close relationship with Huang and his administration's decisions on export controls.The administration has opened the door for Nvidia to do business in China, while Trump has repeatedly defended its approach to export restrictions against criticism. These decisions have come under scrutiny as the company faces questions over its China-related business and the allegations surrounding Huang.White House officials have repeatedly maintained that Trump does not personally select or trade individual stocks. The president has also rejected calls to sell his stock holdings.According to the White House, Trump's assets are held in a trust managed by his children, while independent financial managers handle his investment portfolio.Trump has also appeared to question his administration's assessment of Alice Huang's alleged links to Chinese intelligence.“I don’t know that she’s a spy at all. Nobody's proven that,” he told reporters outside the White House on Monday. “He probably shouldn’t have been doing, on a personal basis, what he did. You know, from — who knows? That's a different story. But nobody's proven that she's a spy. She may not be a spy,” he said.Nvidia shares were trading at around $157.72 on Monday, down more than 3.1% during the day. The decline came as investors reacted to Huang's resignation ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings call scheduled for Tuesday.Huang stepped down last Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, who is suspected of being a spy.
Article Summary: Trump's investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year. Financial disclosures suggest that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.

Article Title: India faces 'acute' aircraft shortage, needs more than 1,000 planes: Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
Union minister Piyush Goyal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India is looking to add another 1,000 civilian aircraft to its existing orders as it struggles to keep up with rising air traffic demand amid an "acute" shortage of planes, Union minister Piyush Goyal said.The government is also pushing established aircraft manufacturers to speed up supplies.Speaking to reporters during his two-day visit to Egypt, Goyal said expanding the aircraft fleet would help improve air connectivity between the two countries and create room for more flights."We need to see more (air) connectivity... as we get more aircraft, we are sure we will be able to have more flights to Egypt," he said.Goyal is in Egypt to explore opportunities to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries. Currently, EgyptAir operates direct flights connecting India and Egypt.Pointing to the scale of India's aircraft requirements, the minister said the country had already ordered more than 1,200 planes but would need over 2,000 aircraft to meet its requirements. It is now prepared to place orders for another 1,000 planes, while pressing manufacturers to ensure quicker deliveries."We have ordered more than 1,200 planes, and we are ready to order another 1,000 planes; we need more than 2,000 planes for our requirements.So we are pursuing the established manufacturers of aircraft for faster supplies," Goyal said.He reiterated that the arrival of more aircraft would allow Indian airlines to operate additional flights to Egypt.India is one of the world's fastest-growing civil aviation markets, with airlines IndiGo and Air India having placed substantial aircraft orders with Airbus and Boeing for deliveries in the coming years.The country is also seeing the presence of several major international aerospace companies. Airbus has two final assembly lines in India, catering to military transport aircraft and helicopters.Global aircraft manufacturers Boeing and Airbus also source components and services worth around $2 billion every year from India. Meanwhile, Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer has partnered with the Adani Group under a strategic collaboration to explore setting up regional aircraft manufacturing in India.
Article Summary: India is looking to add another 1,000 civilian aircraft to its existing orders. The government is also pushing established aircraft manufacturers to speed up supplies. Union minister Piyush Goyal is in Egypt to explore opportunities to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries.

Article Title: Smartphones, TVs, refrigerators and daily essentials set to get costlier after Diwali as companies pass on rising input costs; handset prices have already risen over 40% this year
Article Text:
The pressure is mounting on fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) manufacturers. (Image for representative purpose only)

Daily essentials to cost more

Electronics prices to go up

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It’s time to prepare for a squeeze on your household budgets as companies prepare to hike prices with the Diwali festive season over. Consumer goods companies are gearing up for another round of price increases across smartphones , televisions, refrigerators and daily-use products as they grapple with rising input costs and seek to safeguard their margins.With the festive season now behind them, manufacturers are looking to recover the accumulated cost burden through higher retail prices and reductions in product grammage, potentially adding to the pressure on household budgets.The pressure is mounting on fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) manufacturers. Companies in the sector are preparing to raise prices to offset increases in the cost of refined palm oil, sugar, milk and packaging laminates, all of which became up to 7% more expensive sequentially in the previous quarter.Britannia Industries has signalled additional price increases and cuts in pack sizes for its Rs 5 and Rs 10 products. Tata Consumer Products has also increased prices of salt, sauces and condiments, with the revised rates expected to reach the market soon. These moves come after Amul raised milk prices and ITC increased cigarette prices last week.Britannia chief executive Rakshit Hargave told ET that the company had implemented a 3.5% price increase in the previous quarter, while also reducing the quantity in fixed-price packs.“There is more price increase in activation which is in the works,” he told analysts earlier this month. “It is going to come, and that is something that we have to do.”Samsung and Xiaomi, two major smartphone brands, raised prices of their handsets and tablets by up to 18% over the weekend. Xiaomi announced a separate increase of up to 7% in television prices on Monday. Appliance manufacturers Haier and Godrej have also raised prices by up to 7% across their product ranges.“Raw material prices continue to remain elevated and sustaining profitability is becoming an issue,” Haier India chief executive Satish NS was quoted as saying by the financial daily. “Sales are growing healthily upwards of 20%, but profits are taking a bad hit.”He noted that the industry's previous round of across-the-board price increases took place in September. Most listed consumer goods companies had reported pressure on margins in the first half of FY27 as commodity prices continued to climb. They were unable to pass on the entire increase in costs to buyers because they wanted to protect demand.Companies now expect the next round of price increases to improve profitability by transferring the full impact of higher costs to consumers.The latest round of increases comes as consumer demand faces fresh challenges, particularly in the smartphone segment. Kailash Lakhyani, chairman of the All India Mobile Retailers Association, said mobile phone sales by volume have fallen 40% after Diwali compared with the corresponding period last year. This follows a 20% year-on-year decline during Diwali itself, after multiple rounds of price increases over the course of this year.“The current price increases will further dent demand,” he said. “Getting a sub-20,000 5G phone has now become difficult, which will badly impact sales.”Industry executives expect electronic brands across the board to raise prices over the coming 7-10 days.If implemented, the impending increases would take the total price rise this year to more than 40% for smartphones, over 20% for televisions and 15-20% for household appliances.Kamal Nandi, business head (appliances) at Godrej Enterprises Group, said manufacturers had consciously held back the increases until the festive season was over.The factors driving higher costs differ across product categories.Smartphone and television manufacturers are dealing with a sharp rise in memory chip prices, as demand from AI infrastructure continues to exceed available supply.Appliance makers, by contrast, are contending with higher commodity and freight expenses. FMCG companies are facing mounting costs of edible oil, sugar, milk and packaging materials.
Article Summary: The pressure is mounting on fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) manufacturers. Companies in the sector are preparing to raise prices to offset increases in the cost of refined palm oil, sugar, milk and packaging laminates. Britannia Industries has signalled additional price increases and cuts in pack sizes for its Rs 5 and Rs 10 products.

Article Title: $7 billion green boost: Amazon invests big in India's renewable energy landscape
Article Text:
Amazon to pour in $7 billion in India's wind and solar energy projects by 2030

Company targets 65% reduction in electricity-related carbon intensity

57 renewable energy projects across India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amazon is set to pump an additional $7 billion into renewable energy projects in India by 2030, taking its investments in the country's carbon-free energy sector further as it expands its wind and solar power portfolio.The fresh investment comes on top of the $4 billion in renewable energy projects that the company has already contracted in India. Amazon said its existing projects, once operational, will have the capacity to generate enough electricity to meet the annual requirements of more than 3.5 million Indian households.According to the company's statement, Amazon has signed agreements for four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts (MW). The projects are spread across Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.Karnataka will host two of these projects, including a 234 MW wind farm and a 200 MW project combining solar and wind energy. The wind farm is Amazon's largest wind energy project contracted in Asia so far. The other projects comprise a 300 MW solar facility in Madhya Pradesh and a 200 MW solar project in Rajasthan.The projects are backed by power purchase agreements, which involve long-term commitments to purchase electricity generated by specific renewable energy facilities.They are part of Amazon's existing $4 billion contracted investment in the country. Once operational, the company's contracted projects will have a combined capacity of more than 2 gigawatts (GW).Amazon said the planned $7 billion investment would also contribute to its broader efforts to reduce the carbon intensity of electricity used across its global operations.Alongside its India investment announcement, Amazon has set a global target to bring down the carbon intensity of electricity powering its operations by 65% by 2030.This means the carbon emissions associated with each unit of electricity consumed by the company will be 65% lower than the levels recorded in its 2019 baseline.The target is part of Amazon's efforts towards meeting its Climate Pledge commitment of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2040. The company said the goal comes at a time when global energy demand is growing.Commenting on the investment, Kara Hurst, Amazon's chief sustainability officer, said, “Our renewable energy investments in India reflect years of sustained effort, planning, and collaboration across the industry. This additional investment of $7 billion underlines our long-term commitment, helping bring additional wind and solar capacity online while contributing to India’s energy security and long-term renewable energy ambitions,”Hurst added, “By expanding access to renewable energy at scale, we aim to help meet India’s growing electricity demand, strengthen the country’s energy security, and contribute to its ambitious goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.”Amazon's renewable energy presence in India extends beyond utility-scale projects. Its current portfolio comprises 14 large-scale wind and solar projects that feed carbon-free electricity into the grid, along with 43 solar installations at its own facilities.Together, these 57 projects contribute to the company's efforts to increase the availability of carbon-free electricity and expand renewable energy capacity in the country.The investments are also expected to support electricity supply beyond Amazon's own operations. New carbon-free energy projects add power to the grid that serves households, hospitals, educational institutions and businesses.The expansion of renewable energy projects also supports the modernisation of energy infrastructure, helps maintain stable and affordable electricity access over time and contributes to job creation and better grid reliability.Increasing investments in carbon-free energy and grid infrastructure can also help scale new technologies, encourage innovation and strengthen the wider energy ecosystem.
Article Summary: Amazon has signed agreements for four new wind and solar projects with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts. The projects are spread across Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. They are part of Amazon's existing $4 billion contracted investment in the country.

Article Title: Foreign investors may increase bets on Indian financial stocks as flows recover: Jefferies
Article Text:
Representative image

Foreign ownership in BSE 500 hits 12-year low

FPIs remain underweight in several sectors

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have considerable scope to increase their exposure to India's financial sector, as their holdings in the segment remain below the five-year average, brokerage firm Jefferies said in a report.The assessment comes as foreign investment flows into Indian equities have turned positive since mid-October, with net buying reaching $11.4 billion so far. Of this, FPIs bought shares worth $9.6 billion in November so far, alongside a sharp rally in banking stocks.Jefferies said the relatively low positioning of overseas investors in financial stocks leaves room for further buying as foreign flows recover.“Financials relative positioning for FPIs is below average, leaving room for catch-up,” the brokerage said.According to the report, at the end of the September 2026 quarter, FPIs' relative overweight position in financials was 2.3 percentage points below the five-year average and 6.2 percentage points below the peak recorded in March 2023.The recent return of foreign buying follows two years of outflows, which brought FPI ownership in the BSE 500 to a 12-year low of 17.3% as of September 2026, Jefferies said.In contrast, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) increased their shareholding in the BSE 500 to 18.8%, the highest level in 12 years, supported by sustained inflows.Promoters held a 48.5% stake in the index, down two percentage points from the peak recorded in June 2024. Direct individual ownership remained unchanged at 8.5%.The brokerage also highlighted the role of non-India-dedicated active funds, which accounted for 63.8% of the total $691 billion in FPI assets under custody as of September 2026.Jefferies said these funds could raise their allocations to Indian equities given their relatively light positioning.Beyond financials, foreign investors were overweight in healthcare by 0.2 percentage points and real estate by 0.1 percentage points.However, they remained underweight across other sectors, with the largest gaps in energy at 1.7 percentage points, consumer staples at 1.3 percentage points and consumer discretionary at one percentage point.The report said large-cap stocks had led the latest market rally. Since mid-October, the Nifty 100 has gained 9%, compared with a 4% rise in mid-cap stocks and a 2% increase in small-cap stocks.Among large-cap companies, 60% of those with an FPI-to-DII ownership ratio above one outperformed the Nifty 100, Jefferies said.The brokerage said a sustained recovery in foreign investment flows could benefit large-cap stocks disproportionately. It reiterated its preference for large-cap shares over small- and mid-cap stocks.
Article Summary: Foreign investment flows into Indian equities have turned positive since mid- October. FPIs bought shares worth $9.6 billion in November so far, alongside a sharp rally in banking stocks. Recent return of foreign buying follows two years of outflows, which brought FPI ownership in BSE 500 to a 12-year low.

Article Title: Gold hit a lifetime high near Rs 1.80 lakh per 10 grams in January 2026; 10 months later, MCX gold is down about 25% while silver has crashed nearly 60% from its Rs 4.20 lakh/kg peak
Article Text:
Higher interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, which does not generate income, making the precious metal less attractive to investors. (Image for representative purpose only)

Gold price crash

:

Gold And Silver Fall in Numbers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At the start of 2026, investors of gold and silver were a happy lot. Ten months later, gold and silver prices have crashed spectacularly from their lifetime highs. Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday but continued to hover close to a more-than-one-year low recorded in the previous session, as a stronger US dollar and rising expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month weighed on the precious metal.The metal had fallen to its lowest level since October 2025 on Monday. US gold futures for December delivery also advanced, rising 0.6% to $3,876.70 per ounce.Also Read | Predicted to hit Rs 2 lakh, will gold prices fall to Rs 1.25 lakh per 10 grams? The dollar climbed to a fresh 19-month high on Tuesday, making gold priced in the US currency costlier for buyers using other currencies.Among other precious metals, spot silver advanced 1.1% to $47.50 per ounce after touching its lowest level since late October 2025 in the previous session.Platinum prices rose 1.2% to $1,467.29 per ounce, while palladium gained 0.8% to $976.58.In the domestic market, MCX Gold is currently trading at Rs 1,34,884 per 10 grams down 0.4% so far this year and 25.4% or Rs 45,895 below its lifetime high of Rs 1.8 lakh.MCX Silver, currently at Rs 1,69,292, has declined 28.2% year to date and is 59.7% or Rs 2,50,756 below its lifetime high of Rs 4.2 lakh per kg.According to CME's FedWatch tool, markets are pricing in a 95.4% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase in December.The likelihood of a larger, 50-basis-point hike stands at 4.6%.Higher interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, which does not generate income, making the precious metal less attractive to investors.Investors are now looking to the minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest Open Market Committee meeting, scheduled for release on Wednesday, for indications of the likely direction of US monetary policy."Gold is trading as a function of expectations for US Fed policy next year and the market trying to work out how high interest rates in the States can go," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com."Essentially, the big selloff we saw last night in gold is a reflection of that and today's bounce is just a slight reversal of it,” Rodda was quoted as saying by Reuters."Demand has stayed resilient so far, but mounting macro headwinds could erode investment demand, leaving the market without a key pillar of support," analysts at ANZ said in a note."Silver remains a high-beta play on gold. With its own demand fundamentals soft, any sustained rebound will depend on a gold recovery," the note added.Gold prices have retreated from the record highs reached in January this year, with several factors contributing to the decline.The initial slide came as investors booked profits after the metal climbed to elevated levels, triggering a sharp fall in prices. Before gold could find its footing, the US-Iran war broke out, pushing crude oil prices above $120 per barrel and intensifying concerns over inflation.More recently, a sharp and unprecedented rise in real yields has put gold under considerable selling pressure. The US Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. With inflation remaining elevated, expectations of further rate increases in the coming months have also strengthened.The shift in the Fed's stance, from considering rate cuts to raising interest rates, has supported the US dollar. Higher yields have made US bonds more appealing to investors, increasing the opportunity cost of holding gold. Since the precious metal does not pay interest, its attractiveness diminishes when investors can earn higher returns from bonds.
Article Summary: Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday but continued to hover close to a more-than- one-year low. A stronger US dollar and rising expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month weighed on the precious metal. Spot silver advanced 1.1% to $47.50 per ounce after touching its lowest level since late October 2025 in the previous session.

Article Title: North Bengaluru expansion puts focus on low-density residential projects
Article Text:
Fewer homes, more room

A clubhouse sized for the community, not the render

Connected, without sitting in the traffic

A record behind the address

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

North Bengaluru has emerged as a key area of the city’s expansion over the past decade. Developments around the airport, Metro connectivity, Manyata Tech Park and Phoenix Mall of Asia have contributed to the corridor’s growth, alongside an increase in residential development. As the area has expanded, there has also been growing interest in residential options that offer greater privacy and lower-density living.According to Krishnaiah Projects Pvt Ltd, Bollineni Vienna at Kogilu Cross in Yelahanka is planned around this demand for lower-density living. The company states that the project comprises over 80 residences spread across 2.65 acres, with two towers rising to G+18 floors. Krishnaiah Projects Pvt Ltd is the real estate arm of the 52-year-old Bollineni Group (BSCPL), according to the company.The company states that the residences are available in 4 and 5 BHK configurations, ranging from 3365 to 5510 sq ft. Tower A has two homes per floor; Tower B has three. No residence shares a common wall with another, and a private elevator opens directly into each home. Layouts are 100 per cent Vastu-compliant. Close to 80 per cent of the site is left open, landscaped ground rather than built mass.“Ninety homes on 2.65 acres was a decision we took early and have not revisited,” says TV Manjunath, CEO. “Almost everything residents will value here, the open space, the privacy, the light through the day, follows from that one number. It is easier to add amenities later than to add distance between homes.”According to the company, the 25,000 sq ft clubhouse is planned as shared ground rather than an amenity list. It includes a double-height badminton court, a paddle pool, a gymnasium, a meditation deck, a jogging track, lawn tennis and pickleball courts, and a children's play area. A lounge and gathering plaza anchors the social side. The Herbarium and the Skyline Perch — a landscaped terrace and an elevated viewing deck — extend the community upward as well as outward.Kogilu Cross sits off Bellary Road, with the Outer Ring Road and Kempegowda International Airport both within a straightforward drive. Manyata Tech Park and Hebbal serve the working commute; Phoenix Mall of Asia and Yelahanka Junction cover the everyday one. The location gives access to North Bengaluru's infrastructure without placing residents inside its busiest stretches.Bollineni's real estate division has been building since 2012, averaging close to one and a half homes a day over that period.That pipeline sits against a broader shift in how buyers at this end of the market assess a home. Convenience, well-being and work-life balance have moved closer to location in the order of priorities, and low-density planning is one of the few ways a developer can answer all three at once.
Article Summary: Bollineni Vienna at Kogilu Cross in Yelahanka is planned around this demand for lower-density living. The project comprises over 80 residences spread across 2.65 acres, with two towers rising to G+18 floors. Close to 80 per cent of the site is left open, landscaped ground rather than built mass.

Article Title: Meta tightens Instagram content recommendations in India amid government scrutiny
Article Text:
Representative image

Government flags risks from recommendation systems

Meta faces wider scrutiny over content on its platforms

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Meta Platforms has modified Instagram 's recommendation systems in India to reduce the amount of sexually suggestive and violent content shown to users, as the government steps up oversight of online platforms and their content policies.The changes, announced by the company on Tuesday, apply to recommendations from accounts that users do not follow. Meta said they affect what Instagram promotes rather than imposing a blanket ban on the content itself, according to Reuters.The announcement comes after the Indian government asked Meta last month to review how its systems recommend posts and strengthen checks on material that could incite violence or disrupt public order.Meta said it had improved its default protections over the past year in response to user feedback. It also said people in India now report seeing recommended content about half as often as they did a year ago, but did not provide figures to support the claim.The company did not directly link the latest changes to the government's advisory.In an advisory dated October 10, the ministry of electronics and information technology asked Meta to review its ranking and recommendation systems to ensure that potentially misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material was not disproportionately amplified.The ministry also asked the company to ensure users were not disproportionately exposed to a single narrative or a limited set of viewpoints, and to report the measures taken to address these concerns, according to Reuters.The government's concerns extend beyond the content hosted on social media platforms to the systems that determine what users see.The advisory sought greater scrutiny of how recommendation mechanisms amplify material and shape users' exposure to different narratives.The latest changes come amid broader scrutiny of Meta's handling of harmful content, including child sexual exploitation material, on Facebook and Instagram.Last month, Meta said that it had taken action against 5.3 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content on its platforms in India between January and June 2026. More than 98% of the material was detected proactively, the company said, according to news agency PTI.Meta also said it had introduced additional measures to strengthen its efforts to tackle such content.The disclosure followed government concerns over the company's handling of child sexual abuse material and its responsibilities as an intermediary.Officials had warned that Meta could risk losing the legal protections, commonly referred to as safe harbour, available to intermediaries if it failed to meet its obligations.The government had also raised concerns about the role of Meta's recommendation and advertising systems, arguing that these mechanisms gave the company responsibilities beyond simply hosting content posted by users.Separately, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights had warned Meta representatives during an inquiry into alleged advertisements linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material on the platform.Meta India chief Arun Srinivas and other senior executives appeared before the panel as part of the inquiry.Meta has previously changed content-ranking systems on Facebook in countries including Canada and Brazil to reduce the amount of political content recommended to users.
Article Summary: The changes apply to recommendations from accounts that users do not follow. The Indian government asked Meta last month to review how its systems recommend posts and strengthen checks on material that could incite violence or disrupt public order. The government's concerns extend beyond the content hosted on social media platforms to the systems that determine what users see.

Article Title: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney dies at 95; started global chain with $600 loan from mother
Article Text:
Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney.

Who was Dan Carney?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Wichita State pays tribute

Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney, who turned a $600 loan from his mother into one of the world's biggest pizza chains alongside his brother Frank, has died at the age of 95.Carney died peacefully on November 13, surrounded by his family, according to an obituary published by his family. No cause of death was disclosed. The New York Post reported his death on Monday, citing the obituary.Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University.The venture took off despite pizza being relatively unfamiliar to many American diners at the time. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.In 1977, PepsiCo acquired Pizza Hut for $300 million. Frank, who had served as the company's CEO, left the position in 1980. He died in December 2020 at the age of 82 after battling pneumonia.Born in Kansas City, Missouri, Carney grew up in a large family and was one of 12 siblings, according to the NYP. He graduated from Wichita State University in 1953 with a bachelor's degree in business administration.He subsequently served two years in the US Air Force as a first lieutenant before returning to his academic pursuits.He received his master's degree in 2004, 51 years after completing his undergraduate studies.Carney married his childhood sweetheart, Beverly Singleton, in February 1954. The couple had six children and 12 grandchildren. Beverly died in 1998. Carney later married Gayla Coulter in 2001, and she survives him.Beyond his business career, Carney was involved in philanthropy and served as chairman of the board of the Cerebral Palsy Research Foundation of Kansas for 50 years.His obituary described him as a leader known for his integrity, generosity and commitment to mentoring others.“Dan was revolutionary in the franchise world,” the obituary said, adding that he was an investor not just in businesses but also in people.Wichita State University, Carney's alma mater, also paid tribute to the entrepreneur, recalling his contribution to the institution and the wider community.In a Facebook post on Monday, the university described him as an entrepreneur, philanthropist and proud Shocker whose impact would be felt for generations.The university also highlighted his humility, wisdom and belief in giving back, saying his mentorship had shaped the lives of students and colleagues.The original Pizza Hut building, where the brothers launched their business, has been preserved on the Wichita State campus. It now houses the Pizza Hut Museum, which opened to the public in 2018.Carney had attended the museum's opening and described seeing the original building as a humbling experience, according to a Wichita State University press release.
Article Summary: Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.

Article Title: EU slaps anti-dumping duties on steel imports from India, 4 other countries
Article Text:
India faces a 9.5% EU anti-dumping duty on cold-rolled flat steel, while Japan, Taiwan, Türkiye and Vietnam also face duties

Why India and Taiwan were flagged

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Scale of EU steel market

The European Union on Monday imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of cold-rolled flat steel from India and four other countries, with rates ranging from 3% to 27.9%. This follows an investigation that found the products were being sold in the EU at dumped prices.India faces a duty of 9.5%, while Japan has been hit with the highest rate of 27.9%. The duties on Taiwan range from 20.7% to 27%, those on Türkiye from 3% to 7.8%, and Vietnam faces a 16% duty.The European Commission said the investigation was significant because it was the first in which it established the existence of what it calls “particular market situations” in some of the countries under investigation. It said the findings could have wider implications for the EU's trade defence measures.The Commission established particular market situations in India and Taiwan, saying domestic market conditions in both countries affected the prices used to assess whether steel was being dumped in the EU.In India's case, it found that government measures had affected domestic iron ore prices. Iron ore is a key raw material used in the production of cold-rolled flat steel, as per an EU report.For Taiwan, the Commission cited the impact of Chinese overcapacity. It said increased imports of cold-rolled flat steel from China had put downward pressure on domestic prices and weakened profitability for Taiwanese producers.Under EU anti-dumping rules, the Commission can construct a product's normal value instead of relying on domestic selling prices when it finds that market conditions do not allow a proper comparison between domestic and export prices.The Commission said it had taken corrective measures and that the investigation revealed the full extent of dumping in the EU market.Cold-rolled flat steel is used across several manufacturing sectors. The EU market for these products is valued at around 23.2 billion euros, with domestic production spread across 12 member countries and employing more than 8,600 people.The Commission's statement puts the value of imports from the five countries at 1.072 billion euros. Taiwan accounted for 345 million euros, followed by India at 282 million euros, Türkiye at 240 million euros, Japan at 180 million euros and Vietnam at 125 million euros.The EU said the duties are intended to protect its domestic steel industry from trade-distorting practices.
Article Summary: India faces a duty of 9.5%, while Japan has been hit with the highest rate of 27.9%. The duties on Taiwan range from 20.7% to 27%, those on Türkiye from 3% to 7.8%, and Vietnam faces a 16% duty. Cold-rolled flat steel is used across several manufacturing sectors.

Article Title: Anthropic is eyeing a mega IPO, but will investors buy its trillion-dollar AI dream?
Article Text:
Anthropic's trillion-dollar IPO dream

Tech IPO scorecard: Big gains, bigger setbacks

Revenue is soaring, but so are the costs

More shares could enter the market from day one

AI investment faces the returns question

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Will Anthropic's IPO be a market blockbuster or another case of early fireworks fading fast?The Claude parent’s proposed $1.4 trillion listing comes at a time when recent technology IPOs have delivered sharply contrasting returns, leaving investors with little indication of what could lie ahead.An analysis by S&P Global Market Intelligence of seven major recent US technology IPOs found that four were trading above their offer prices a year after listing, while the other three had suffered significant losses. The contrasting returns offer little certainty about how Anthropic's shares will perform if its proposed Nasdaq listing goes ahead.The AI company plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece, according to an amended registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10. At the upper end of the price band, the offering could fetch $64.35 billion, placing Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at around $1.4 trillion. Its shares are expected to trade under the ticker ANT.This would put the company above its $965 billion valuation from a May funding round, although below the approximately $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for earlier this year.The first-year performance of recent listings has been far from uniform.Arm Holdings topped the S&P analysis, delivering a 171.4 per cent return after its September 2023 listing. Snowflake and Airbnb were not far behind, gaining 169.6 per cent and 165.3 per cent, respectively. DoorDash also posted a positive return of 61.6 per cent.The picture was less encouraging for Lyft, Uber and Rivian. Their shares fell 62.6 per cent, 29.7 per cent and 57.7 per cent, respectively, amid market disruptions and rising interest rates.Even some of the biggest recent offerings have struggled to maintain their initial momentum. SpaceX, which raised $135 per share in June in the largest IPO on record, witnessed a surge in its stock during the first two trading sessions. However, the rally subsequently lost steam.On June 18, its shares dropped 6.5 per cent as investors booked profits and weighed the company's high valuation against the costs of expanding its AI operations. By November 11, the stock was 13.2 per cent below its offer price, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix also saw early gains give way to a correction after its Nasdaq debut in July. Its American depositary receipts (ADRs), which were priced at $149, rose 12.8 per cent on the first trading day before falling nearly 8 per cent on the second as investors booked profits.Anthropic's financial numbers present another important consideration ahead of its proposed market debut. The company reported revenue of $33.24 billion in the first nine months of 2026, significantly higher than the $4.58 billion recorded for the whole of 2025.Its third-quarter revenue stood at around $17 billion, registering a 47 per cent increase over the previous quarter. However, the revenue growth comes alongside substantial losses and infrastructure spending.Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. Its infrastructure commitments stood at around $895 billion, including $69.8 billion payable within 12 months.The number of shares available for trading could also become a point of focus after the listing. Anthropic's employees and early investors will be allowed to sell some of their holdings from the first day of trading, instead of being bound by the standard 180-day lock-up period.There is also another component to the IPO's funding arrangements. Seven of the company's computing suppliers have agreed to buy a combined $26 billion worth of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price.Anthropic's proposed debut comes as investors take a closer look at whether massive investments in artificial intelligence are translating into revenue at the pace expected.Recent third-quarter earnings have brought capital expenditure and the ability of companies to generate returns from AI spending into sharper focus. Regulatory uncertainty following the US midterm elections has added another concern for the sector.With recent technology listings showing that first-day excitement does not always guarantee sustained stock market gains, Anthropic's proposed IPO will bring its valuation, financial losses and infrastructure commitments under investor scrutiny.
Article Summary: Anthropic plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece. At the upper end of the price band, the offering could fetch $64.35 billion. This would put Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at around $1.4 trillion.

Article Title: Debt, dues and deja vu: How poor nations end up paying more than they borrow
Article Text:
Developing countries' external debt hits record $9.4 trillion

Countries pay more than they receive

Poorest countries face highest borrowing costs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Private lending and bond sales pick up

The debt burden on low and middle-income countries continues to rise, with repayments becoming more expensive and fresh loans costing more. Their external debt reached a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, as countries paid more towards existing loans than they received in new funding. Borrowing costs also hit their highest levels in decades for some of the poorest economies, according to a World Bank report.The World Bank's International Debt Report 2026 said external debt increased 5.5 per cent from $8.9 trillion in 2024. This was the biggest annual rise since 2021. The increase was driven by higher borrowing, a recovery in lending from private lenders and a weaker US dollar, which raised the reported value of debt.The growing debt has increased the amount countries need to spend on repayments. In 2025, low- and middle-income countries spent $1.4 trillion on servicing their debt, which includes both principal and interest payments. This was 1.9 per cent more than in 2024 and the fifth consecutive annual increase.The amount paid towards debt was also much higher than the fresh funding received. Between 2022 and 2025, these countries paid around $436.1 billion more in debt repayments than they received in new financing.Payments to bondholders alone rose 13.7 per cent to $363.1 billion in 2025.Highlighting the pressure on poorer nations, the World Bank said, “The countries that can least afford it are paying the most to borrow.”Countries eligible for funding from the International Development Association (IDA) faced particularly high borrowing costs. They paid an average interest rate of 8.2 per cent on new loans in 2025, the highest level since the late 1980s.Borrowing money from bondholders was even more expensive, with interest rates averaging 9.4 per cent during the year.However, the trend was different for countries borrowing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Their average interest rate fell to 5.5 per cent in 2025, compared with 5.8 per cent in 2024.Lending by private creditors to developing economies also increased in 2025. The debt owed by low- and middle-income countries to private lenders rose 5.2 per cent to $5 trillion.Governments also raised more money through bond sales. Public-sector bond issuances jumped 34.6 per cent to $250.6 billion, the highest level since 2021, the report said.This activity has continued in 2026.Preliminary figures for January to August show that countries continued to issue bonds despite high borrowing costs. Several countries had already issued more bonds in the first eight months of 2026 than they had during the whole of 2025.The World Bank warned that rising debt repayments and high funding needs are leaving governments with less money to manage their finances. This is also increasing the risks linked to rising debt and the need to refinance existing loans.
Article Summary: Developing countries' external debt hits record $9.4 trillion in 2025. Countries paid more towards existing loans than they received in new funding. Borrowing costs also hit their highest levels in decades for some of the poorest economies. World Bank warned that rising debt repayments and high funding needs are leaving governments with less money to manage their finances.

Article Title: Intel sued by shareholders after stock plunges 29% in a single day, wipes out $140 billion
Article Text:
The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations

Why shareholders have sued Intel

Intel shares remain under pressure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Intel has been hit with a shareholder lawsuit accusing the US chipmaker of concealing mounting problems in its personal computer business, weeks before a disappointing financial forecast triggered a massive stock sell-off that wiped out nearly $140 billion in market value in a single day.The proposed class-action lawsuit, filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, on Friday, alleges that Intel misled investors by failing to disclose the extent to which slowing PC sales and an inventory glut were weighing on its business. The company's shares plunged 28.6% on October 30, marking their steepest single-day decline in decades and one of the biggest blows to its market valuation.The lawsuit has been brought by shareholders led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, a Michigan pension fund. Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and chief financial officer David Zinsner have also been named as defendants. The plaintiffs are seeking unspecified damages on behalf of investors who purchased Intel shares between July 23 and October 29.According to the complaint, Intel was too slow to inform investors about the impact of weakening PC demand and excess inventory on its revenue prospects. Shareholders argued that these problems outweighed the potential gains from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, including increased investment in data centres.The lawsuit also alleges that Intel had both the motive and opportunity to defraud investors when it raised capital in mid-August, halfway through what the plaintiffs described as a 'disastrous' third quarter. The company sold $23 billion worth of stock at $95 per share as it sought to expand its chip contract manufacturing business, a key component of Tan's strategy.The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations. The following day, its shares crashed 28.6%, erasing approximately $140 billion in market value.During an earnings call, Tan expressed disappointment over manufacturing supply shortages, an 'unprecedented memory crunch' and the resulting weakness in PC demand.'We need to address these challenges with urgency,' he told analysts.Intel has invested heavily in expanding its manufacturing capabilities, hoping to capitalise on growing demand for chips used in AI data centres. However, supply disruptions have made it difficult for the company to benefit fully from that demand. At the same time, rising memory prices have pushed up PC costs, further weighing on consumer demand.The October sell-off has continued to cast a shadow over Intel's stock, even as the broader market has shown signs of resilience. The company's shares came under renewed pressure during the following trading sessions, falling further amid a wider rout in semiconductor stocks.According to Yahoo Finance calculations, chip and memory companies collectively lost more than $400 billion in market value in a single session during the recent downturn. Intel was among the biggest casualties, with its market value falling sharply from its September levels.Intel shares closed at $59.66 on Friday, November 13. Despite the recent losses, the stock remains up 62% so far this year, although it has retreated significantly from its June 30 peak of $142.35.
Article Summary: The proposed class-action lawsuit alleges that Intel misled investors by failing to disclose the extent to which slowing PC sales and an inventory glut were weighing on its business. The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations. The following day, its shares crashed 28.6%, erasing approximately $140 billion in market value.
